summary.short: Uruguayan statute on cybercrime: adds offences to the Penal Code, requires the Executive to promote a national educational campaign on cybersecurity and personal finance, and lets financial institutions and e-money issuers share fraud registries and freeze funds in disputed transfers. Promulgated 23/08/2024.
summary.long: Statute on the prevention and repression of cybercrime. Chapter I adds offences to the Penal Code (arts. 277-TER, 288-BIS to 288-TER, 297-BIS to 297-QUATER, 347-BIS, 347-TER, 348-BIS, 348-TER, 358-QUATER, 358-QUINQUIES, 359-TER) and amends Ley 19.574 art. 34 numeral 34; the reproduced text gives only these amendment notes, not the text of the added articles. Chapter II requires the Executive Power to promote a national educational campaign on personal finance and cybersecurity in specified secondary and technical education centres and for beneficiaries of listed public programmes, covering payment means, bank accounts, credit, phishing, vishing, smishing, malware, trojans and social engineering. Chapter III authorises financial intermediation institutions and electronic-money issuers to create inter-institutional registries of data on unauthorised transactions, and disapplies the limits of Decree-Law 15.322 for sharing those records among themselves and with judicial authorities. Chapter IV authorises these institutions not to execute withdrawal or transfer orders on accounts receiving funds from disputed transactions, up to the disputed amount; requires notice to the Banco Central del Uruguay within one business day; and lists cases in which the freeze must be lifted, including no complaint filed within 48 hours or no court order within 30 days. Penalties for the added offences are not stated in the reproduced text.

notes: The document contains Arts. 1 to 11 in four chapters. Arts. 1 to 8 consist only of editorial notes stating which Penal Code and Ley 19.574 articles were added; the wording of those new offences is not in the document and is not annotated here. The amendment relations rest on these database notes, not on operative text of this law. Arts. 10 and 11 are permissive ('Facúltase'); the only duties stated are the one-business-day communication to the BCU and the 48-hour and 30-day deadlines in Art. 11, which belong in the events section. The document contains no penalty or enforcement provisions for this law. Registry title writes 'Ley N° 20.327'; the document header writes 'Ley N° 20327'. Entities for the classes 'instituciones de intermediación financiera' and 'entidades emisoras de dinero electrónico' are recorded as one class-level row because the text does not name individual firms. The section_status entries for relations and entities are given only because the schema requires them; both sections contain entries above.

obligations.summary: The Executive Power shall promote a national educational campaign on personal finance and cybersecurity in specified public education centres and beneficiary programmes, with content to be reviewed and updated periodically. Competent entities shall also run digital-security campaigns nationwide, ensuring equal access to ICT and gender equity.

evidence.quote: El Poder Ejecutivo promoverá una campaña nacional educativa sobre el manejo de finanzas personales y ciberseguridad

obligations.summary: Financial intermediation institutions and electronic money issuers are empowered to create inter-institutional registers of data to identify, manage and prevent unconsented transactions and fraudulent operations, and to share these registers with judicial authorities for filing complaints, without the limits of Decree-Law 15.322.

evidence.quote: Facúltase a las instituciones de intermediación financiera y a las entidades emisoras de dinero electrónico a crear registros interinstitucionales

obligations.summary: Financial intermediation institutions and electronic money issuers are empowered to refrain from executing withdrawal or transfer orders on accounts that received funds from transactions declared unauthorised by the originating account holder; the freeze covers current balances and future inflows up to the disputed amount.
obligations.conditional_on: when they have become aware, by reliable means, that funds from disputed transactions entered the accounts

evidence.quote: Facúltase a las instituciones de intermediación financiera y a las entidades emisoras de dinero electrónico a la no ejecución de cualquier tipo de orden de retiro o transferencia de activos

obligations.summary: A fund freeze under Art. 11 must be communicated to the Banco Central del Uruguay (BCU) within one business day; the BCU may request additional information and may order the freeze lifted. The freeze must be lifted and the BCU notified where the conditions listed in literals A to D occur (no complaint filed within 48 hours, no judicial confirmation within 30 days, judicial lifting order, or convincing evidence from the account holder).
obligations.conditional_on: when a fund freeze has been imposed under Art. 11

evidence.quote: deberá ser comunicada dentro del plazo de un día hábil al Banco Central del Uruguay (BCU)

obligations.summary: Financial intermediation institutions and electronic money issuers must execute any order exceeding the limit of the disputed transaction amounts, unless the order fails to meet legal or contractual requirements.
obligations.conditional_on: for orders exceeding the amount of the disputed transactions, unless the orders do not meet legal or contractual requirements

evidence.quote: debiendo las instituciones de intermediación financiera y las entidades emisoras de dinero electrónico ejecutar toda orden que excediera dicho límite

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changes legal treatment. The only numbers are procedural time limits (one business day for BCU notice in Art. 11; 48 hours and 30 days in Art. 11 A-B), which are events, not thresholds. Art. 11 ties the freeze to the disputed transaction amount without a numeric value. Art. 9 sets no numeric limits.

definitions.note: Art. 9 K defines phishing, vishing, smishing, malware, troyano and ingeniería social, but only as content for the educational campaign, not to set scope or legal consequence. Art. 1-8 insert offences into the Penal Code, but their text is not reproduced in this document, only the insertion notes. Art. 10-11 refer to 'instituciones de intermediación financiera' and 'entidades emisoras de dinero electrónico' without defining them in this text.

enforcement.note: Arts. 1-8 insert new offences into the Código Penal (arts. 288 BIS, 288 TER, 277 TER, 347 BIS, 348 BIS, 358 QUATER, 359 TER, 297 BIS-QUATER, 347 TER, 348 TER, 358 QUINQUIES) and Art. 4 into Ley 19.574. This text does not state the penalties for these offences, and it contains no fines, licence revocation, benefit clawback, suspension or blocking as sanctions. Art. 11 freezes funds on accounts as a preventive measure, not as a penalty. Art. 10 authorises shared registers of offenders, which is not a sanction.
